item.title: Pensacola Artist AKWtheartist Opens Exhibition at Museum of Culture & Heritage
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola-area artist Aaron Waters, professionally known as AKWtheartist, will showcase his imaginative approach to illustration and character design at the Museum of Culture & Heritage starting Friday, December 11. The opening reception runs from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at the museum's location on East Church Street and will feature original artwork, a…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola-area artist Aaron Waters, professionally known as AKWtheartist, will showcase his imaginative approach to illustration and character design at the Museum of Culture & Heritage starting Friday, December 11. The opening reception runs from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at the museum's location on East Church Street and will feature original artwork, a multimedia presentation, and an opportunity to meet Waters and discuss his creative process.

Waters, a Pace High School graduate who studied at the Savannah College of Art and Design, creates visual worlds that blend exaggerated figures, fantastical characters, and illustration styles inspired by video games and animation. His portfolio was selected for the Florida State Fair's Wall of Excellence in 2022. The exhibition runs through December 19 and represents a contemporary addition to the museum's programming.

The opening reception will also offer a one-night-only opportunity to purchase limited-edition prints of selected work. Admission details were not provided in the event announcement. For more information, the Museum of Culture & Heritage can be found on Instagram and Facebook.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola FC has qualified for the 2027 US Open Cup as the national champions, according to an announcement from The League For Clubs on Bluesky. The competition kicks off in April 2027.

The Pensacola club will be joined in the tournament by FORO SC and Napa Valley 1839 FC, which qualified through The League For Clubs pathway. The US Open Cup is the top annual soccer tournament in the United States, open to professional and semi-professional clubs.

This marks another significant milestone for Pensacola FC, which has established itself as a competitive force in the domestic soccer landscape.

item.title: Escambia County Commissioner's Son Killed in Apparent Deliberate Shooting at Blackwater River Campsite
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: An Escambia County commissioner's son has been killed in what authorities are investigating as a deliberate shooting rather than a hunting accident, according to reporting from WJHG. The incident occurred while the victim was camping along the Blackwater River. According to accounts cited in the report, witnesses say shooters were close enough to…
item.content:encoded:
An Escambia County commissioner's son has been killed in what authorities are investigating as a deliberate shooting rather than a hunting accident, according to reporting from WJHG.

The incident occurred while the victim was camping along the Blackwater River. According to accounts cited in the report, witnesses say shooters were close enough to see the campfire and hear people talking before opening fire repeatedly. The shooting was followed by additional volleys, and witnesses report the shooters laughed as they drove away from the scene.

The Escambia County Sheriff's Office is investigating the incident. Details on a suspect or suspects have not yet been released. This remains an active investigation.

item.title: Pensacola Beach Turkey Trot Expands Fundraising Efforts to Help Local Foster Children

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Beach, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - Runners taking part in this year's Thanksgiving morning Turkey Trot on Pensacola Beach will be helping support an additional local cause.

The annual event, now in its 16th year, has traditionally raised money for brain cancer research. Organizers are expanding their charitable efforts this year to include Children in Crisis, a Northwest Florida nonprofit that helps foster children and families.

The event takes place Thursday at Casino Beach, beginning with a children's race at 8 a.m. The 5K will follow at 8:30 a.m.

The Turkey Trot has become a Thanksgiving tradition for local residents and visitors looking to get some exercise before their holiday celebrations while supporting charitable causes.

More information about the event, registration and race details is available at PensacolaBeachTurkeyTrot.com.

item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - A Thanksgiving tradition spanning more than seven decades will continue Thursday as Waterfront Mission prepares to serve approximately 1,600 free holiday meals across its Pensacola and Mobile locations. This is the organization's 77th annual Thanksgiving lunch, bringing together staff, kitchen workers and more than…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - A Thanksgiving tradition spanning more than seven decades will continue Thursday as Waterfront Mission prepares to serve approximately 1,600 free holiday meals across its Pensacola and Mobile locations.

This is the organization's 77th annual Thanksgiving lunch, bringing together staff, kitchen workers and more than 130 volunteers.

The meals are intended for individuals and families throughout the community, including those struggling financially and those who might otherwise spend Thanksgiving alone.

Waterfront Mission has a long history of providing food, shelter and other assistance to people experiencing homelessness and hardship along the Gulf Coast.

The Pensacola mission is located at 348 West Herman Street.

Additional information about Waterfront Mission, its services and opportunities to support the organization's work is available at WaterfrontMission.org.

The Florida Vibe will join five other teams in the league when it begins play in 2027, making it the PSL's sixth franchise. The announcement marks a significant addition to Pensacola's sports landscape and represents another investment in the community by Studer, who has been instrumental in developing local entertainment and economic initiatives.

item.title: Nearly $46 Million Contract Awarded to Advance Pensacola Superfund Cleanup
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - The long-running effort to clean up the former Escambia Wood Treating Company property in Pensacola is taking another major step forward. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers announced Monday that it has awarded a $45.7 million contract to Parsons Government Services to address contamination at the Superfund site. The…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - The long-running effort to clean up the former Escambia Wood Treating Company property in Pensacola is taking another major step forward.

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers announced Monday that it has awarded a $45.7 million contract to Parsons Government Services to address contamination at the Superfund site.

The former wood treatment facility operated from 1942 until 1982, leaving behind environmental contamination that has required decades of cleanup efforts.

The latest contract will focus on reducing groundwater contamination, with the initial phase involving detailed planning before fieldwork begins.

The Army Corps of Engineers will oversee the work in coordination with the Environmental Protection Agency. The contract covers a five-year period.

Federal officials say removing creosote from the groundwater is an important step toward eventually returning the property to productive use as the proposed Midtown Commerce Park.

The cleanup represents another milestone in efforts to address longstanding environmental concerns while creating new economic development opportunities in Escambia County.

item.title: Pensacola Sets December 1 Groundbreaking for Long-Awaited Hollice T. Williams Park Project
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - After decades of discussion and planning, construction is about to begin on a project that will transform the area underneath Interstate 110 in Pensacola. The city will hold a groundbreaking ceremony for the Hollice T. Williams Stormwater Park project at 8:30 a.m. Tuesday, December 1. The first phase of…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - After decades of discussion and planning, construction is about to begin on a project that will transform the area underneath Interstate 110 in Pensacola.

The city will hold a groundbreaking ceremony for the Hollice T. Williams Stormwater Park project at 8:30 a.m. Tuesday, December 1.

The first phase of construction will include an elevated trail system, resurfaced athletic courts, landscaping and improvements designed to help manage stormwater.

Future phases will focus on improving connections between neighborhoods, adding park amenities and expanding the Long Hollow Pond area.

The project encompasses approximately 34 acres and stretches 1.3 miles beneath the interstate.

The area was once home to hundreds of African American families, churches and businesses before construction of I-110 displaced the neighborhood in the late 1960s. The park is intended to honor that history while creating new recreational opportunities.

Funding includes $25.1 million in federal disaster recovery money, $5 million in Deepwater Horizon restoration funding and up to $1.8 million from the Florida Department of Transportation.

Residents can learn more about the project and view design plans at HTWPensacola.com

item.title: Pensacola Humane Society slashes adoption fees for holiday adoption event
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Humane Society is joining a nationwide push this December to get more animals into homes during the holiday season. From December 1–5, the shelter will slash adoption fees to just $49 through BISSELL Pet Foundation's "Empty the Shelters Holiday Hope" event, a significant discount from typical rates. The program is designed to ease…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Humane Society is joining a nationwide push this December to get more animals into homes during the holiday season. From December 1–5, the shelter will slash adoption fees to just $49 through BISSELL Pet Foundation's "Empty the Shelters Holiday Hope" event, a significant discount from typical rates.

The program is designed to ease capacity pressures shelters face year-round. All adopted pets come spayed or neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped. Blake White, CEO of Pensacola Humane Society, said the reduced fees make it easier for local families to open their homes during the holidays. "If you've been thinking about adopting, come spend some time with our dogs and cats," White said. "Our staff and volunteers know them well and would love to help you find the right match."

The Empty the Shelters event is running nationally from December 1–11 across 263 animal welfare organizations in 36 states. Since its launch in 2016, the initiative has helped more than 445,000 pets find homes. Prospective adopters should contact Pensacola Humane Society directly for details on the adoption process and available animals.

item.title: Santa Rosa County's Economic Development Success Raises Questions About Escambia's Approach
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - Santa Rosa County's success in attracting major employers is prompting discussion about how neighboring Escambia County approaches economic development. The Pensacola News Journal reports some local business leaders believe Escambia County could benefit from streamlining its business recruitment process, pointing…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - Santa Rosa County's success in attracting major employers is prompting discussion about how neighboring Escambia County approaches economic development.

The Pensacola News Journal reports some local business leaders believe Escambia County could benefit from streamlining its business recruitment process, pointing to Santa Rosa County's economic development department as a potential model.

Santa Rosa County has secured more than $50 million in Triumph Gulf Coast funding and attracted several major employers, including Leonardo Helicopters, Buffalo Rock and Mondelez International, with an economic development staff of just four people.

Meanwhile, several of Escambia County's major Triumph funding requests have been archived, including requests related to OLF-8 in Beulah and a manufacturing research facility at Pensacola State College.

FloridaWest CEO Chris Plate defended Escambia County's approach in an interview with the News Journal, saying its existing structure provides access to a wider range of financing options and resources.

Escambia County hired former Florida Power and Light executive Rick Byars earlier this year to help coordinate economic development, recruit businesses and secure grant funding.

Santa Rosa County is also pursuing a land swap with the Navy that could open nearly 700 acres near Interstate 10 and State Road 87 for development.

Santa Rosa County Economic Development Director Shannon Ogletree estimates the property could eventually support as many as 2,000 jobs. The land swap has not been finalized.

item.title: Escambia Sheriff's Office Plans to Have Drones Available on Every Shift
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - The Escambia County Sheriff's Office is looking to expand its use of drones, with the goal of having the technology available to deputies on every shift. Sheriff Chip Simmons said Tuesday on NewsRadio's Pensacola Morning News that his department has approximately a dozen drones. He says the technology has helped…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) - The Escambia County Sheriff's Office is looking to expand its use of drones, with the goal of having the technology available to deputies on every shift.

Sheriff Chip Simmons said Tuesday on NewsRadio's Pensacola Morning News that his department has approximately a dozen drones. He says the technology has helped deputies in three or four cases over the past couple of weeks.

Drones equipped with infrared technology have proven particularly useful at night, allowing deputies to locate fleeing suspects more quickly while reducing the risks associated with searching for them on the ground.

Simmons says drones can save deputies considerable time during searches that previously relied heavily on officers establishing perimeters and waiting for suspects to emerge.

The sheriff's office has shared several videos demonstrating how drones have assisted deputies in recent investigations.

Simmons says the department is committed to expanding the program and making the technology available during both daytime and overnight shifts.

item.title: Coffee Shop Burglar Caught on Camera, Now in Custody
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: An armed burglary suspect is now in custody after being clearly identified on surveillance camera footage from a coffee and soda shop on Archer Road, according to Sheriff Simmons. The suspect, captured on video wearing a white hooded jacket, made no attempt to avoid the business's security cameras during the incident. Sheriff Simmons noted the…
item.content:encoded:
An armed burglary suspect is now in custody after being clearly identified on surveillance camera footage from a coffee and soda shop on Archer Road, according to Sheriff Simmons.

The suspect, captured on video wearing a white hooded jacket, made no attempt to avoid the business's security cameras during the incident. Sheriff Simmons noted the suspect's visibility on the footage played a key role in the arrest.

The individual now faces multiple charges including burglary, larceny, and dealing in stolen property. The arrest highlights the importance of surveillance systems in solving retail crimes and protecting local businesses in the Pensacola area.

Sheriff Simmons discussed the case during Tuesday's Pensacola Morning News interview, emphasizing how surveillance technology continues to aid law enforcement in apprehending perpetrators. The footage provided clear identification that assisted deputies in locating and taking the suspect into custody.

This case is part of ongoing efforts by the Escambia County Sheriff's Office to combat property crime affecting local businesses. Store owners are encouraged to maintain updated surveillance systems and report any suspicious activity to law enforcement.

The investigation is ongoing. Anyone with additional information regarding this incident is asked to contact the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

item.title: Woman on Probation Arrested Again with Illegal Firearm
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A woman currently on probation for a prior felony firearm possession conviction was arrested Tuesday after being caught carrying another illegal gun, according to Sheriff Chip Simmons. The arrest occurred at approximately 3:30 a.m. when deputies approached the suspect. Upon seeing law enforcement, the woman fled the scene and discarded a backpack…
item.content:encoded:
A woman currently on probation for a prior felony firearm possession conviction was arrested Tuesday after being caught carrying another illegal gun, according to Sheriff Chip Simmons.

The arrest occurred at approximately 3:30 a.m. when deputies approached the suspect. Upon seeing law enforcement, the woman fled the scene and discarded a backpack containing the firearm.

The suspect now faces additional charges for violating the terms of her probation, Simmons said during an interview on the Pensacola Morning News.

The arrest underscores ongoing law enforcement efforts to remove illegal weapons from the streets and hold repeat offenders accountable. Sheriff Simmons emphasized the department's commitment to addressing firearm violations and protecting the community.

The case highlights challenges faced by probation officers in monitoring individuals with histories of gun-related offenses. Violations of probation conditions can result in significant legal consequences, including potential incarceration.

Details regarding the specific charges and the suspect's court appearance were not immediately available. The case remains under investigation.

This arrest is part of continued efforts by the Escambia County Sheriff's Office to combat illegal firearms possession in the community.

item.title: Santa Rosa Sheriff Warns of Holiday Dangers as Fatal Shooting Under Investigation
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County Chief Deputy Randy Tifft is urging residents to stay safe this Thanksgiving as law enforcement investigates a fatal shooting at a remote camping site and addresses multiple criminal cases. A woman in Navarre has been accused of stealing her child's prescribed ADHD medication for personal use and sale. Chief Deputy Tifft said she…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County Chief Deputy Randy Tifft is urging residents to stay safe this Thanksgiving as law enforcement investigates a fatal shooting at a remote camping site and addresses multiple criminal cases.

A woman in Navarre has been accused of stealing her child's prescribed ADHD medication for personal use and sale. Chief Deputy Tifft said she was "doing a little bit of both. She was selling it and using it herself and not giving it to the child." The child has been referred to the Department of Children and Families for placement.

Tifft said the woman "belongs in jail" and faces "a whole list of charges" including child neglect, drug theft, and drug sales.

In a separate incident, authorities are investigating a fatal shooting that occurred overnight at a remote area along Coldwater Creek in northern Santa Rosa County. A camper was killed by gunfire from a vehicle across the creek, according to Tifft.

"There was a vehicle. And again, this is all very new and under investigation. There were some shots fired from across the creek from a vehicle and ended up hitting one of the individuals that was camping," Tifft said.

The shooting appears to have no known altercation preceding it. "We don't think there was, no, there was no altercation. We don't know why that vehicle was shooting a gun in that time of night in that area," Tifft explained.

The remote location required specialized response efforts. "We had to get to them through with boats and canoes to get to them," Tifft said. The investigation remains active, with authorities dedicating all available resources.

As the holiday approaches, Tifft emphasized the importance of safe celebrations. "Don't be drinking and driving this Thanksgiving. There's nothing to celebrate that you need to drive. If you're going to drink, stay home," he said.

Tifft also encouraged residents to avoid family conflicts during gatherings. "Don't get into any disagreements. Everybody get along this Thanksgiving, be thankful for each other, and we don't want any disturbances or any problems. Separate yourself from it," he said.

Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office personnel will be working through the holiday to maintain public safety.
